page: Microsoft Azure B2ls_v2 is an entry-level burstable virtual machine belonging to the Bsv2 series, characterized by a low-memory profile. The instance is provisioned with 2 burstable vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core on an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. Memory is configured at 4.0 GB of RAM, equating to 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware capabilities include instruction set extensions such as AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, and SHA_NI. The instance includes no bundled local storage and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring reliance on remote managed storage and standard Azure networking components.

Benchmark results highlight the constraints of its two-thread, single-core topology alongside burstable scheduling. Single-threaded metrics fall squarely in the average tier, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1632.0 and stress-ng single-core output of 1891.08. Conversely, multi-threaded evaluations reflect lower computational capacity, generating a Geekbench multi-core score of 1887.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 2999.09. Memory operations deliver large-block read throughput of 15.3 GB/sec and write throughput of 14.13 GB/sec. Application tests register 2.02 million Redis SET operations per second and 3.67 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the B2ls_v2 offers an economical resource footprint designed for variable workloads that do not continuously saturate CPU resources. Because CPU credits govern bursting potential, prolonged high-intensity computation is unsuited for this profile. The machine is best fitted for low-traffic web applications, microservices, light background workers, dev-test environments, and low-concurrency internal tools.
description: Microsoft Azure B2ls_v2 is a low-memory, burstable virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. The instance supplies 2 burstable vCPUs spanning 1 physical core, 4.0 GB of RAM, and architectural support for AVX-512 and cryptographic hardware extensions. It contains no local storage and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark testing indicates mid-tier single-threaded execution with a Geekbench single-core score of 1632.0, alongside restrained multi-core performance reflected by a PassMark CPU score of 2999.09 and large-block memory read speeds of 15.3 GB/sec. With its burstable compute allocation and compact memory capacity, the B2ls_v2 provides an economical operational tier suited for intermittent or lightweight tasks such as code development, staging environments, low-throughput web hosting, and basic background queue processing.
